services.summary: A return that matches what the department already knows about you – and that you understand before it's signed.
intro: The Income Tax Department now sees most of your financial life before you file: salary, interest, dividends, share trades, property purchases, high-value spending. A return that doesn't match that data is the most common reason people get notices. So every return we prepare starts with your Annual Information Statement (AIS) and Form 26AS, and ends only when the numbers agree – or the difference is explained.

Two laws, one transition. Income earned up to 31 March 2026 is still taxed under the Income-tax Act, 1961. Income from 1 April 2026 falls under the Income-tax Act, 2025, which replaces 'assessment year' and 'previous year' with a single 'tax year'. Your filings and your planning are handled under the right law for each year.

faqs.q: When is the income tax return due?
faqs.a: If your accounts don't need an audit, the due date has generally been 31 July after the financial year ends. Audit cases have later dates. The government notifies – and sometimes extends – these dates, so the applicable date is confirmed each year.

faqs.q: My income is below the taxable limit. Should I still file?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Filing lets you claim TDS refunds, carry forward losses, and keep a record that banks and embassies ask for. In some cases – large deposits, high foreign travel spend, large electricity bills – filing is compulsory regardless of income.

faqs.q: What happens if my return doesn't match my AIS?
faqs.a: The return may be processed with an adjustment, or you may get a notice asking you to explain. That's why the AIS is reconciled before filing, not after.

faqs.q: I missed the due date. What now?
faqs.a: A belated return can still be filed within the time the law allows, with a late fee and interest where applicable. Some benefits, like carrying forward certain losses, may be lost. After that, an updated return may be possible, with additional tax.

faqs.q: Which law applies to the return I'm filing now?
faqs.a: Returns for income earned up to 31 March 2026 are filed under the 1961 Act. The first returns under the 2025 Act will be for tax year 2026-27 – income earned from 1 April 2026.
